high.title: April IPCA rises 0.67% and accumulates increase of 4.39%, within expectations
high.summary: Brazil's official inflation accelerated in April, with IPCA rising 0.67% monthly, exactly in line with market expectations. The 12-month accumulated inflation reached 4.39%, up from 4.14% in March, approaching the upper limit of the Central Bank's tolerance band of 4.5%. The inflation target remains at 3% with a 1.5 percentage point tolerance margin in either direction. The main driver was Food and beverages, which rose 1.34% and contributed 0.29 percentage points to the index, followed by Health and personal care. This result is crucial for BCB monetary policy decisions, as inflation is now testing the upper bound of the tolerance range. The acceleration suggests potential pressure for tighter monetary policy if the trend continues. FX and bond traders should monitor whether this prompts more hawkish BCB rhetoric and potential Selic rate adjustments in upcoming COPOM meetings.

high.title: Market reacts to Petrobras (PETR4) R$ 9 billion JCP and IPCA; Ibovespa in dollar falls
high.summary: Brazilian markets are digesting Petrobras' Q1 2026 results showing net profit of R$ 32.7 billion, down 7.2% year-over-year. The state oil giant approved R$ 9 billion in shareholder remuneration (R$ 0.70 per share) as advance payment for 2026, to be distributed in two equal installments of JCP (interest on equity) in August and September. Ex-rights trading begins June 2nd with record date June 1st. The market is also processing the April IPCA inflation data. This combination of major SOE earnings and inflation figures significantly impacts the Ibovespa and BRL dynamics. Petrobras' dividend policy and earnings performance directly influence portfolio flows and the broader equity market sentiment, while IPCA results feed into BCB policy expectations affecting both FX and fixed income markets.

medium.title: Itaúsa (ITSA4), Petrobras (PETR4), Raízen (RAIZ4) and other highlights this Tuesday (12)
medium.summary: Itaúsa reported Q1 2026 recurring net income of R$ 4.49 billion, up 17% year-over-year, with ROE reaching 20.1% versus 17.4% in Q1 2025. The holding company's performance reflects strong results from Itaú Unibanco (+11%) and non-financial investments (+76%). As a major banking sector player, Itaúsa's results provide insight into Brazilian financial sector health and potential impacts on bank lending and capital flows.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4): Company's ADRs oscillate in New York despite R$ 9 billion in JCP and oil price rise
medium.summary: Petrobras ADRs showed mixed performance in NYSE pre-market despite announcing R$ 9 billion JCP distribution and rising oil prices due to Middle East conflicts. Brent crude rose 3.55% to $107.89/barrel while WTI gained 3.79% to $101.80. The disconnect between rising oil prices and flat ADR performance suggests market focus on earnings decline rather than commodity tailwinds, relevant for cross-border capital flows and BRL dynamics.

medium.title: The 4 pillars supporting Vale (VALE3) in Empiricus dividend portfolio
medium.summary: Vale returned to Empiricus' automated dividend portfolio in May after reporting Q1 2026 net profit of R$ 1.9 billion, up 29% year-over-year. The mining giant's base metals division showed strong performance, supporting its inclusion in dividend-focused strategies. As a major Ibovespa component and export-driven company, Vale's performance influences both equity indices and Brazil's trade balance dynamics.
